title: Fever and rigidity after starting an antipsychotic — recognising and responding to a time-critical presentation

blocks.text: Fever and rigidity after starting an antipsychotic — recognising and responding to a time-critical presentation
AMaC MRCP PACES23 · R5-201 · Station 2, acute consultation · Skills A–G (focus C, E, F, G) · 20 minutes · Prepared 14 October 2026 · Educational simulation; not an official PACES mark scheme.

A 29-year-old started a dopamine-blocking antipsychotic several days ago. They are now febrile, confused and markedly stiff. Speak to the patient (and accompanying person if applicable), identify immediate risks and explain your management plan. The examiner may provide results on request.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: HOOK — Suspected neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS); serotonin toxicity often has hyperreflexia and clonus, but overlapping or atypical presentations occur. Sepsis remains an essential differential.

TRAP — Marked hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability, altered consciousness and rising CK can herald organ failure. Do not dismiss as anxiety or wait for CK before stopping the offending medicine.

rows: “I need to check how unwell you are first.”
ABCDE, observations, immediate escalation as needed.
“Your symptoms can signal a serious medical complication.”

Medication start/dose changes, dopamine antagonist use, serotonergic agents, agitation, autonomic symptoms; assess temperature, consciousness, generalised rigidity, reflexes and clonus; check infection features.
“We will act while tests are underway.”

Stop suspected dopamine-blocking drug, urgent ABCDE and senior/critical care review; check CK, renal function, electrolytes, ECG, urine myoglobin where indicated, infection screen. Support with fluids, temperature control and monitor for rhabdomyolysis/AKI.
“I will tell you what we are monitoring closely.”
Marked hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability, altered consciousness and rising CK can herald organ failure. Do not dismiss as anxiety or wait for CK before stopping the offending medicine.

Manages hyperthermia, IV fluids with monitoring, renal/electrolyte complications and thromboembolism risk; explains that drug treatment is supportive care first, with specialist-guided adjuncts such as dantrolene or bromocriptine in severe cases

Orders CK, U&E, renal function, FBC, glucose, ECG and infection work-up as indicated

Communicates uncertainty, treatment priorities and need for later psychiatric medication review; explains that antipsychotic rechallenge has a recurrence risk and is deferred to specialist psychiatry after full recovery (typically at least two weeks, low-potency agent, slow titration)

blocks.text: Patient is alert enough for brief conversation unless the scenario worsens. Initially anxious; asks “Am I going to be all right?” Share the presenting details when asked. If the candidate dismisses symptoms, express concern that symptoms are worsening. For a deterioration curveball, become confused or collapse; examiner then supplies observations.

Q1. Why suspect NMS rather than anxiety?
Model: Fever, marked rigidity, altered mental state and autonomic disturbance soon after dopamine antagonist exposure are dangerous.

Q2. What drug changes matter?
Model: Recent antipsychotic initiation or dose increase and other dopamine blockers or dopamine agonist withdrawal matter.

Q3. What do you do immediately?
Model: Stop the suspected precipitant, assess ABCDE, summon acute/critical care support and treat complications.

Q4. How do you distinguish serotonin toxicity?
Model: Serotonin toxicity more often has clonus and hyperreflexia; these syndromes and sepsis may overlap.

Q5. Does a normal early CK exclude NMS?
Model: No. Treat the clinical emergency; CK supports assessment and monitoring but must not delay action.

FAIL — “Keep taking the antipsychotic until the creatine kinase is back.”
PASS — “The combination of fever, rigidity and confusion after a new medicine is serious. Stop that medicine and arrange emergency assessment now.”
HIGH-PERFORMANCE — “We must also check for infection and other emergencies, monitor heart rhythm, kidney function and temperature, and treat complications while involving critical care.”

THINK: Fever and rigidity after starting an antipsychotic. SAY: take symptoms seriously. DO: ABCDE, tests and timely treatment. NUMBERS: 20-minute simulated consultation. TRAP: Marked hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability, altered consciousness and rising CK can herald organ failure. Do not dismiss as anxiety or wait for CK before stopping the offending medicine. FINISH: escalation and monitoring.
BMJ Best Practice: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (reviewed 2026) — https://bestpractice.bmj.com/topics/en-us/990 — consulted 14 October 2026 for the principal clinical decisions.

Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry, 14th edition (2021) — supports: supportive care first with specialist-guided adjuncts (dantrolene, bromocriptine) in severe cases, and deferral of antipsychotic rechallenge to specialist psychiatry after full recovery.
